subject: CR: Logging controls & header masking — post-demo action items
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@cardio360.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Apr 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: CR: Logging controls & header masking — post-demo action items

Hi Anna,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — great discussion. As promised, quick recap focused on the logging/redaction topics you raised and proposed next steps so we stay aligned with your security team.

High-level takeaways from our call:
- Cardio360 priority: avoid storing raw PII in request/response logs (especially in headers/cookies) and retain only pseudonymized traces for troubleshooting.
- You want the ability to mask specific headers (e.g., Authorization, Cookie, X-User-Email) and to control retention windows per environment (staging/prod).
- You asked about trace ID correlation (trace IDs are useful for debugging but should not be linkable to PII without explicit mapping).

Proposed immediate deliverables (ownership + ETA):
1) Redaction matrix draft (what we redact vs pseudonymize) — Ben will produce by Fri 4/10.
2) Sample masked log export (sanitized request/response lines with header examples) — Ben attached sample to his follow-up.
3) Security compliance note (SOC2 scope, KMS usage, audit logs) — Rishi will confirm by Mon 4/13.
4) 30-minute follow-up to walk the redaction matrix and agree on retention — propose Mon 4/12 10:00 AM PT (please confirm).

Attachments: I attached the questionnaire you sent earlier and will circulate the other artifacts once Ben has the sample logs ready.

Open questions for you:
- Can you share a short list of headers/fields you consider sensitive (just names is fine)?
- Do you have a required maximum retention for request logs (e.g., 30 days, 90 days)?

Thanks — we want to make these artifacts discrete so your security team can review quickly.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
[Attachment: Cardio360_Security_Questionnaire_v3.pdf]

From: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@cardio360.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: security@cardio360.com
Date: Thu, 08 Apr 2026 12:02:18 -0700
Subject: Re: CR: Logging controls & header masking — post-demo action items

Thanks Lauren — that summary is perfect. A few clarifying items from the Cardio360 security team: 

- We cannot accept raw request or response bodies in logs that include PHI/PII (names, emails, medical identifiers). If Redwood retains request/response payloads for debugging, they must be redacted before long-term storage.
- Trace IDs: we want them in logs for correlation, but they must not be directly resolvable to patient identifiers without a separate, auditable mapping.
- Headers: please confirm whether Redwood can apply pattern-based masking (regex) for header values and drop entire headers if requested.
- Retention: baseline requirement is 30 days for troubleshooting logs; longer retention (90+ days) requires a business case + encrypted storage and stricter access controls.

We'll compile a short list of sensitive header names and send by EOD tomorrow — thanks for putting the matrix together. Also, Ben, would appreciate the masked log sample for our internal review.

Anna Lopez
Head of IT Security, Cardio360
anna.lopez@cardio360.com
[security@cardio360.com]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@cardio360.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CR: Logging controls & header masking — post-demo action items

Anna — appreciate the clear guidance. Quick technical responses and what I'm attaching: a short masked log extract and a redaction-pattern example.

1) Header masking: yes — Redwood supports both drop and mask actions per-header. We accept a list of header names and regex patterns; matching values are replaced with <REDACTED> or a deterministic token depending on your preference. Examples:
   - Drop: Authorization, Set-Cookie (configurable)
   - Mask: X-User-Email: regex to replace local-part, keep domain if requested

2) Request/response bodies: by default we do NOT persist full bodies for hosted customers. For customers that enable body logging for debugging, we offer an ingestion-time sanitizer stage that applies JSON path redaction rules before any storage.

3) Trace IDs: we keep trace IDs in logs but can pseudonymize them with HMAC-based tokens so the value is stable for correlation but not reversible by operators without a key. That key is KMS-backed and audit-logged.

4) Retention controls: retention is configurable per environment. Default hosted policy is 30 days for request logs; we can extend to 90/365 with additional controls (access gating, encryption-at-rest with customer-managed keys).

Attached: cardio360-masked-log-sample.txt (sample lines from a masked request/response), and a redaction-patterns.txt snippet.

Proposed follow-up: Mon 4/12 10:00 AM PT for a 30-minute walkthrough. If that works for Cardio360, I'll send calendar invite.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
[Attachment: cardio360-masked-log-sample.txt]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@cardio360.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 16:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CR: Logging controls & header masking — post-demo action items

Hi Anna / team — adding a couple compliance-focused clarifications so your auditors have a short note from us.

- SOC2 / Audit posture: Redwood includes request-log ingestion in the scope of our SOC2 Type II report; we use role-based access controls on log viewing and retain an access audit trail. We'll provide the relevant SOC2 section excerpts for your review.
- KMS and encryption: customer-managed KMS is available for stored logs and for the HMAC/pseudonymization keys used for trace IDs. Access to KMS operations is restricted and logged.
- Log retention policy: default hosted request-log retention is 30 days. For Cardio360, if you need 90+ days we recommend customer-managed key storage + narrower RBAC for log read operations.

Next steps (short):
- Ben: share the redaction matrix draft (in-progress).
- Lauren: confirm Mon 4/12 10:00 AM PT or offer alternative.
- Anna/Cardio360: please send the header list and any sticky examples of fields you require removed vs pseudonymized (a one-page list is perfect).
- I will attach a short SOC2 excerpt and a one-pager describing our KMS/HMAC approach after the call.

If useful I can also join the 4/12 call to speak to SOC2 and key management details.

Rishi Malhotra
Security Lead, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
